intro_text: Tonight's quiet summit could end a ten-year trade war - unless a private letter from Ambassador Orlov reaches the press. It went missing from his coat an hour ago, and journalist Pip Harlow is already sniffing around. Recover the letter, find proof of who took it, and return it to the ambassador. If the letter falls into the wrong hands, the summit collapses in scandal.

npc_spawns.inspect_text: A silver-haired diplomat with round glasses. He keeps checking his empty coat pocket.
The ambassador's aide. She notices everything and says very little.
A journalist in a navy blazer, notebook open, pen ready.
The rival envoy, in a dark suit and green tie. He hums along to music no one is playing.
The house valet, who also tunes the piano. He loses things constantly.

item_definitions.inspect_text: A tiny key on a ribbon. It fits the lock on the piano lid.
Ambassador Orlov's private letter, its wax seal unbroken. Thank goodness.
In Envoy Castell's handwriting: 'Harlow - midnight. The letter will be in the piano.'

events.text: Orlov: 'The letter is private - honest words about my own government. If Harlow prints it, the summit is finished.'
Orlov: 'Find it. And find who took it, or they will simply try again.'
Nadia: 'Before dinner I saw Envoy Castell alone by the piano. He closed the lid very quickly when I came in.'
Nadia: 'He was also writing notes in the office. He left some in the bookcase.'
The piano lid is locked. Something rustles inside when you press a key. You need the lid key.
Tomas: 'The piano key? I tie it to the cat's collar so I stop losing it. Clever, yes?'
The cat allows you, just this once, to untie the little key from its collar.
The lid opens. Tucked against the strings is a sealed letter bearing the ambassador's crest.
Between two atlases is a folded note in Castell's hand: 'Harlow - midnight. The letter will be in the piano.'
Castell: 'Fine. I took it. A scandal for Orlov is a victory for me. Do what you must.'
Castell: 'Diplomacy is a game, my friend. Some of us simply play it better.'
Castell reads his own handwriting and goes pale. For once, he has nothing clever to say.
Harlow: 'A little bird says there's a story here tonight. Got anything for me? I pay well.'
Harlow snatches the letter with a grin. By morning it is on every front page, and the summit collapses.
Castell thanks you warmly and walks straight to Harlow. The scandal breaks before dessert.
Orlov: 'My letter! But whoever took it is still in this house. Bring me proof of who it was, then give it back to me.'
Orlov takes the letter and burns it in the fireplace. 'And Castell will be leaving early. Thank you, my friend.'
The summit ends with a handshake and a treaty. No one outside this house will ever know how close it came to disaster.
